note: Do not hand-edit. Regenerate with `node vectors.mjs`.

reproducibility.note: Payload and header segments, all Seals, and all policy/lineage values are byte-stable across runs. ES256 signature octets are NOT: P-ECDSA uses a random k per RFC 6979-optional practice, so the third JWS segment of the attestation differs on every run. That is precisely why seal() covers the signing input and not the signature. See property seal-excludes-signature.

properties.claim: ES256 is randomized, so identical claims must still yield an identical Seal.
Canonical serialization sorts members by code unit and preserves array order.
Member order changes the Seal, so divergent parsers cannot silently interoperate.
Seal is SHA-256 over a domain separator and a 0x00 delimiter, not a bare digest.

enforcement.name: root-cap-survives-lying-parent

enforcement.name: slices-are-not-shared
enforcement.description: A sibling agent spending its own full slice must not be charged against another session.
